terms.core_definition: A Cross-Level Interaction is an advanced moderation phenomenon in Multilevel Modeling (MLM) and Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM), formalized by Stephen W. Raudenbush and Anthony S. Bryk (2002; Snijders & Bosker, 2012), occurring when a higher-level macro variable (Level 2, e.g., departmental climate, school funding, national culture) moderates the relationship between a lower-level micro predictor (Level 1, e.g., employee commitment, student effort) and a lower-level outcome (Level 1, e.g., job performance, test scores). In essence, it models random slopes at Level 1 as predicted outcomes of Level 2 covariates.
terms.seminal_citation: Raudenbush, S. W., & Bryk, A. S. (2002). Hierarchical linear models: Applications and data analysis methods (2nd ed.). SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-Level Interaction according to Aguinis et al. (2013).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The two-level mathematical architecture is specified as:
1. Level 1 (Individual Level) Equation:
$$Y_{ij} = \beta_{0j} + \beta_{1j} X_{ij} + e_{ij}, \quad e_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$$
where $Y_{ij}$ is outcome of individual $i$ in group $j$, and $\beta_{1j}$ is the group-specific slope.
2. Level 2 (Group Level) Equations:
$$\beta_{0j} = \gamma_{00} + \gamma_{01} W_j + u_{0j}$$
$$\beta_{1j} = \gamma_{10} + \gamma_{11} W_j + u_{1j}$$
where $W_j$ is the Level 2 moderator, $\gamma_{11}$ is the cross-level interaction coefficient, and $u_{1j}$ is the random slope disturbance.
3. Combined Mixed-Model Formulation:
$$Y_{ij} = \left( \gamma_{00} + \gamma_{01} W_j + \gamma_{10} X_{ij} + \gamma_{11} (X_{ij} \times W_j) \right) + \left( u_{0j} + u_{1j} X_{ij} + e_{ij} \right)$$
4. Centering Decisions: Level 1 predictor $X_{ij}$ must be Centered within Clusters (CWC / group-mean centering: $X_{ij} - \bar{X}_{.j}$) to completely separate pure micro-level slope variance from macro-level contextual between-group variance.
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological benchmarks (Raudenbush & Bryk, 2002; Enders & Tofighi, 2007):
- Centering Rule: When testing cross-level interactions, Group-Mean Centering (CWC) of the Level 1 regressor is mandatory; using Grand-Mean Centering (CGM) conflates within-group and between-group effects, biasing $\gamma_{11}$.
- Sample Size Requirements: Detecting a cross-level interaction requires adequate Level 2 sample size (minimum 30 to 50 groups, with 5 to 20 individuals per group; 50/20 rule).
- Random Slope Verification: The Level 1 slope $\beta_{1j}$ must exhibit significant residual variance ($u_{1j} > 0$ via likelihood ratio test) before modeling Level 2 cross-level predictors.
terms.pitfalls:
Critical multilevel modeling errors:
1. Conflating Centering Strategies: Using Grand-Mean Centering for $X$ when interpreting cross-level interactions, resulting in an uninterpretable blend of individual and contextual influences.
2. Underpowered Level 2 Sample Sizes: Conducting multilevel cross-level moderation with only 10 or 12 organizations ($J = 12$), leading to severely inflated standard errors and high Type II error rates for $\gamma_{11}$.
3. Fixing Slopes to Invariance: Testing $\gamma_{11}$ while constraining the random slope variance to zero ($u_{1j} = 0$), which severely deflates standard errors and causes massive false-positive rejections (Type I errors).
terms.apa_reference: Enders, C. K., & Tofighi, D. (2007). Centering predictor variables in cross-sectional multilevel models: A new look at an old issue. Psychological Methods, 12(2), 121-138. https://doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.12.2.121

terms.vietnamese: Tiêu chuẩn hệ số tải chéo đánh giá giá trị phân biệt
terms.core_definition: Tiêu chuẩn hệ số tải chéo (Cross-Loadings Criterion - Chin, 1998) là phương pháp đánh giá giá trị phân biệt ở cấp độ biến quan sát (chỉ báo) trong mô hình SEM. Tiêu chuẩn yêu cầu hệ số tải nhân tố ngoài (outer loading) của một biến quan sát lên cấu trúc tiềm ẩn mà nó đại diện phải lớn hơn đáng kể so với tất cả các hệ số tải chéo của biến đó lên bất kỳ cấu trúc tiềm ẩn nào khác trong mô hình.
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-loadings criterion according to Henseler et al. (2015); Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Xây dựng bảng ma trận hệ số tải chéo (Cross-loadings matrix) biểu diễn tương quan giữa tất cả các biến quan sát với toàn bộ điểm số biến tiềm ẩn (latent variable scores). 2. Kiểm tra điều kiện từng hàng: Hệ số tải chính lambda_ii phải vượt trội hơn mọi hệ số tải chéo lambda_ij (với j != i). 3. Khoảng cách chênh lệch tối thiểu: Delta_lambda = lambda_ii - max(lambda_ij) phải đạt ngưỡng an toàn.
terms.benchmarks: Ngưỡng Chin (1998) & Hair et al. (2022): Hệ số tải chính phải >= 0.70. Khoảng cách giữa hệ số tải chính và hệ số tải chéo cao nhất tối thiểu phải đạt từ 0.10 đến 0.20 đơn vị. Nếu biến quan sát tải lên một cấu trúc khác với mức độ gần bằng cấu trúc gốc (Delta_lambda < 0.10), biến bị nghi ngờ có tính nhập nhằng (ambiguous item).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Chỉ dựa vào tiêu chuẩn Cross-loadings để bảo vệ giá trị phân biệt trên các tạp chí Q1. Nghiên cứu mô phỏng của Henseler et al. (2015) đã chứng minh rằng Cross-loadings có độ nhạy cực kỳ kém (tỷ lệ phát hiện sai sót dưới 50% trong nhiều kịch bản); bắt buộc phải báo cáo tiêu chuẩn HTMT song hành.
terms.apa_reference: Chin, W. W. (1998). The partial least squares approach to structural equation modeling. Modern Methods for Business Research, 295(2), 295–336.

terms.vietnamese: Nhận diện tải chéo trong phân tích nhân tố
terms.core_definition: Cross-Loadings Identification is an essential diagnostic procedure in Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), and PLS-SEM (Wynne W. Chin, 1998; Joseph F. Hair et al., 2019) that evaluates whether an observed indicator loads substantially on more than one latent construct. In a well-specified reflective measurement model exhibiting clean simple structure (Thurstone), an indicator should have a high primary factor loading on its designated theoretical construct and near-zero cross-loadings on all alternative constructs. Substantial cross-loadings signal item ambiguity, construct contamination, or severe violations of discriminant validity.
terms.seminal_citation: Chin, W. W. (1998). The partial least squares approach to structural equation modeling. Modern Methods for Business Research, 295(2), 295-336.
terms.expert_notes: – Lưu ý: ngưỡng chênh tải chéo <0.2 là quy ước thực hành, nên ghi rõ không phải tiêu chuẩn gốc của Hair
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-Loadings Identification according to Hair et al. (2019).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The diagnostic inspection protocol functions across two primary modeling environments:
1. EFA Pattern & Structure Matrices: In oblique rotation (Promax, Direct Oblimin), inspect the Pattern Matrix. An item has a cross-loading if it loads $\ge 0.32$ or $\ge 0.40$ on two or more distinct factors.
2. Cross-Loading Criterion in PLS-SEM (Chin, 1998): For each indicator, compute its bivariate correlation with all latent variable scores. The indicator's loading on its assigned construct must be greater than all of its cross-loadings on any other construct by a margin of at least $0.10$ (or $0.20$).
3. Modification Indices in CB-SEM: Inspecting covariance residuals and Modification Indices (MI) in CFA; a large MI ($> 10.0$) associated with an unmodeled path from a latent construct to an indicator flags an empirically significant cross-loading.
4. Item Purification: Items with substantial cross-loadings are prime candidates for elimination during scale refinement.
terms.benchmarks:
Established empirical benchmarks (Hair et al., 2019; Tabachnick & Fidell, 2019):
- Minimum Cross-Loading Difference Rule: The primary loading should exceed any secondary cross-loading by at least $0.20$ (e.g., primary $= 0.75$, highest cross-loading $\le 0.55$).
- Primary Loading Threshold: Primary loading should be $\ge 0.708$ (so that $\lambda^2 \ge 0.50$, indicating the construct explains $> 50\%$ of item variance).
- Complementary Discriminant Metric: In PLS-SEM, cross-loadings are reported alongside the Fornell-Larcker criterion and the modern gold standard HTMT (Heterotrait-Monotrait Ratio $< 0.85$).
terms.pitfalls:
Common research reporting errors in SEM manuscripts:
1. Suppressing Cross-Loadings in EFA: Setting SPSS or R display options to 'suppress absolute values $< 0.50$', hiding substantial cross-loadings of $0.45$ from reviewers.
2. Retaining Ambiguous Items: Keeping items that load $0.62$ on Factor 1 and $0.58$ on Factor 2, which corrupts the distinct conceptual identity of both constructs.
3. Confusing Pattern Matrix with Structure Matrix: In EFA with oblique rotation, interpreting cross-loadings from the structure matrix (which includes factor intercorrelations) rather than the pattern matrix (which isolates unique direct contributions).
terms.apa_reference: Hair, J. F., Risher, J. J., Sarstedt, M., & Ringle, C. M. (2019). When to use and how to report the results of PLS-SEM. European Business Review, 31(1), 2-24. https://doi.org/10.1108/EBR-11-2018-0203

terms.vietnamese: Thăm dò trực tuyến đa quốc gia (Web Probing)
vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật thăm dò web xuyên quốc gia
terms.core_definition: Cross-National Web Probing is an innovative, mixed-method survey pretesting methodology developed by Dorothée Behr, Michael Braun, Katharina Meitinger, and colleagues (2012, 2017) that scales up traditional face-to-face cognitive interviewing across multiple languages, nations, and cultures using online, self-administered survey platforms. By embedding targeted open-ended cognitive probes (e.g., category-selection probes, comprehension probes) immediately following substantive survey questions in large online probability or non-probability panels across diverse countries, web probing identifies cross-national measurement equivalence breakdowns, translation errors, and culturally divergent mental models with high statistical power.
terms.seminal_citation: Behr, D., Kaczmirek, L., Bandilla, W., & Braun, M. (2012). Asking web participants about operational thinking: A new approach for cognitive pretesting. Field Methods, 24(3), 282-300. https://doi.org/10.1177/1525822X12442910
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-national web probing according to Wiley / Beatty & Willis (2020); Wiley (2020).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The operational workflow functions across four structured phases:
1. Target Item & Probe Selection: Formulating open-ended cognitive probes targeting known cultural ambiguity zones:
   - Category-Selection Probes: 'Why did you choose [response option]?'
   - Comprehension / Definition Probes: 'What came to your mind when you read the term [concept]?'
   - Specific Probes: 'In your view, does this question include [specific group]?'
2. Parallel Online Fieldwork: Administering identical probed web questionnaires to demographically balanced online panels across target nations (typically $N = 500$ to $1,000$ respondents per country).
3. Cross-National Coding Scheme Development: Developing a cross-cultural coding schema with exhaustive inclusion/exclusion criteria to classify open-ended text answers into thematic categories.
4. Comparative Invariance Analysis: Cross-tabulating coding categories by nation to empirically test whether respondents in different countries comprehended and interpreted the survey question identically.
terms.benchmarks:
Cross-cultural methodological criteria (Behr et al., 2012, 2017):
- Sample Size Power: Employs large samples ($N \ge 500$ per nation), overcoming the small-sample limitations of classical face-to-face cognitive pretesting ($N = 10-15$).
- Cross-Cultural Measurement Invariance: Acts as a qualitative diagnostic companion to quantitative Multigroup CFA invariance testing (explaining *why* metric or scalar invariance failed).
- Non-Response Threshold: Open-ended probe completion rates in web probing typically exceed $80\%$ to $85\%$ when probes are limited to 4–6 per survey.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research design flaws in web probing:
1. Open-Ended Probe Fatigue: Overburdening respondents with 15 open-ended text boxes, resulting in gibberish, copy-pasting, or escalating dropout rates.
2. Machine Translation Coding Failures: Using automated machine translation on foreign language probe responses without engaging native-speaker bilingual coders, missing subtle cultural idioms and slang.
3. Omitting Non-Substantive Codes: Failing to systematically code non-responses, ambiguous responses, and 'Don't know' answers, which often conceal severe question comprehension failure.
terms.apa_reference: Behr, D., Meitinger, K., Braun, M., & Kaczmirek, L. (2017). Web probing: Implementing cognitive interviewing techniques in online surveys. GESIS Survey Guidelines. https://doi.org/10.15465/gesis-sg_en_024

terms.vietnamese: Thiết kế nghiên cứu cắt ngang
vietnamese_variants: Thiết kế cắt ngang trong khảo sát
terms.core_definition: A Cross-Sectional Research Design is an observational empirical research architecture in which data are collected from sample units (individuals, firms, organizations) at a single, discrete point in time (or over a short temporal window). Analyzed in detail by Paul E. Spector (2019) and Aric Rindfleisch et al. (2008), cross-sectional designs are effective for estimating population prevalence, establishing bivariate associations, and testing exploratory correlations with minimal cost and zero participant attrition. However, because independent, mediating, and dependent variables are measured synchronously, cross-sectional designs lack temporal precedence, making them highly susceptible to Common Method Variance (CMV) and fundamentally incapable of establishing definitive causal directionality.
terms.seminal_citation: Rindfleisch, A., Malter, A. J., Ganesan, S., & Moorman, C. (2008). Cross-sectional versus longitudinal survey research: Concepts, findings, and guidelines. Journal of Marketing Research, 45(3), 261-279. https://doi.org/10.1509/jmkr.45.3.261
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-sectional research according to Saunders et al. (2019); Saunders (2019).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The operational execution involves four design components:
1. Sampling Snapshot: Sampling a representative probability or purposive sample from the target population at time $T_0$.
2. Synchronous Variable Measurement: Administering measurement instruments capturing predictors ($X$), potential mediators ($M$), controls ($Z$), and outcomes ($Y$) within the same survey questionnaire or observation session.
3. Correlational & Regression Modeling: Modeling covariances using OLS regression, logistic regression, or structural equation modeling.
4. Procedural Safeguards Against CMV: Implementing psychological separation of items, counter-balancing scale order, varying response formats, and introducing objective marker variables to mitigate common method artifacts.
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological standards (Spector, 2019; Rindfleisch et al., 2008):
- Appropriate Scope: Highly appropriate for mapping demographic prevalence, descriptive epidemiology, testing measurement model properties, and exploratory mapping.
- Explicit Epistemic Humility: High-impact publications explicitly acknowledge causal limitations, phrasing claims in terms of 'associations', 'relationships', or 'correlations' rather than claiming proven causal mechanisms.
- Triangulation with Secondary Data: Cross-sectional survey independent variables should be merged with objective, temporally lagged secondary data (e.g., subsequent firm financial performance from Compustat) to introduce temporal precedence.
terms.pitfalls:
Fatal reviewer criticisms in empirical manuscripts:
1. Asserting Causal Claims from Synchronous Data: Stating that '$X$ causes $Y$' or claiming to have 'proven a mediation sequence $X \to M \to Y$' based on a single cross-sectional survey where all questions were answered in 10 minutes.
2. Inability to Rule Out Reverse Causality: Failing to address whether $Y$ causes $X$ (e.g., whether Job Satisfaction causes Performance, or high Performance causes Job Satisfaction).
3. Fatal Common Method Bias: Measuring sensitive dependent and independent variables through identical self-report scales from the same respondent at the same time, producing inflated, spurious correlations.
terms.apa_reference: Spector, P. E. (2019). Do not cross me: Optimizing the use of cross-sectional designs. Journal of Business and Psychology, 34(2), 125-137. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10869-018-09613-8

terms.vietnamese: Độ dư thừa kiểm thực chéo (Q²)
terms.core_definition: Cross-Validated Redundancy ($Q^2$)—pioneered independently by Mervyn Stone (1974) and Seymour Geisser (1974)—is a foundational sample-reuse predictive relevance metric in Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Computed via the Blindfolding resampling procedure, $Q^2$ evaluates the out-of-sample predictive validity of a structural model by systematically omitting data points from the indicator matrix, re-estimating model parameters, and assessing how accurately the structural model predicts the omitted values. A $Q^2$ value greater than zero confirms that the model possesses genuine predictive relevance for that specific endogenous construct beyond naive sample mean prediction.
terms.seminal_citation: Stone, M. (1974). Cross-validatory choice and assessment of statistical predictions. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 36(2), 111-133. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1974.tb00994.x
terms.expert_notes: Q² (Stone–Geisser, blindfolding) không phải dự báo ngoài mẫu thực sự – dùng PLSpredict (Shmueli et al. 2019) | Trùng #646; LaTeX thô
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-validated redundancy ( Q 2 ) according to Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The blindfolding and computational procedure functions as follows:
1. Blindfolding Omission Distance ($G$): Select an omission distance $G$ (typically $G = 7$, where $5 \le G \le 10$, such that sample size $N$ divided by $G$ is not an integer). The algorithm systematically deletes every $G$-th data point from the endogenous indicators.
2. Iterative Parameter Estimation: The PLS model is estimated on the remaining data points; missing points are predicted using the structural and measurement equations.
3. Sum of Squared Errors Computation: Compute the Sum of Squared Prediction Errors ($\text{SSE}$) and the Sum of Squared Base Errors ($\text{SSO}$, predicting omitted points by the mean of remaining points).
4. Cross-Validated Redundancy Formulation:
$$Q^2 = 1 - \frac{\text{SSE}}{\text{SSO}}$$
In Cross-Validated Redundancy, predictions are generated using both the structural model paths AND the measurement model, whereas Cross-Validated Communality uses only the measurement model.
terms.benchmarks:
Established PLS-SEM benchmarks (Hair et al., 2019; Henseler et al., 2014):
- Minimum Threshold: $Q^2 > 0$ indicates that the model has predictive relevance for the target endogenous construct.
- Effect Sizing Benchmarks:
  - $0 < Q^2 \le 0.25$: Small predictive relevance.
  - $0.25 < Q^2 \le 0.50$: Medium predictive relevance.
  - $Q^2 > 0.50$: Large predictive relevance.
- Modern Evolution (PLSpredict): Modern standards increasingly recommend complementing or replacing blindfolding $Q^2$ with out-of-sample $k$-fold cross-validation (Shmueli et al.'s 2019 PLSpredict, reporting $Q^2_{\text{predict}}$).
terms.pitfalls:
Common methodological traps in PLS reporting:
1. Confusing Redundancy with Communality: Reporting Cross-Validated Communality instead of Cross-Validated Redundancy; communality ignores the structural regression paths entirely and tests only indicator fit.
2. Applying to Formative Endogenous Constructs: Computing $Q^2$ via blindfolding on formatively measured endogenous constructs; blindfolding is psychometrically meaningful only for reflective or composite endogenous indicators.
3. Negative $Q^2$ Concealment: Omitting reporting when $Q^2 < 0$; a negative $Q^2$ demonstrates that naive mean imputation predicts the data better than the complex structural model.
terms.apa_reference: Geisser, S. (1974). A predictive approach to the random effect model. Biometrika, 61(1), 101-107. https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/61.1.101

terms.term: Stone-Geisser's Q² in PLS-SEM (Blindfolding Predictive Relevance)
terms.vietnamese: Hệ số Q² Stone-Geisser trong PLS-SEM (Độ phù hợp dự báo Blindfolding)
vietnamese_variants: Độ phù hợp dự báo Stone-Geisser
terms.core_definition: Stone-Geisser's $Q^2$ in PLS-SEM is the formal operational metric of out-of-sample predictive relevance for endogenous constructs in Partial Least Squares path modeling, established by Mervyn Stone (1974) and Seymour Geisser (1974; Hair et al., 2019). Derived using the non-parametric Blindfolding procedure, $Q^2$ evaluates the parameter stability and predictive capability of the combined structural and measurement model by systematically predicting omitted data points. In PLS-SEM reporting, it serves as the essential bridge connecting in-sample explanatory power ($R^2$) with out-of-sample predictive validity.
terms.seminal_citation: Stone, M. (1974). Cross-validatory choice and assessment of statistical predictions. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 36(2), 111-133. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1974.tb00994.x
terms.expert_notes: Q² blindfolding không phải dự báo ngoài mẫu thực sự (Shmueli et al. 2019); trùng #645 | Trùng #645; LaTeX thô
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-validated redundancy (Q^2) according to Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The operational blindfolding protocol functions through four algorithmic steps:
1. Omission Distance Configuration: Selecting omission distance $D$ (customarily set to $D = 7$), ensuring that $N / D$ is a non-integer to guarantee that every data point is omitted exactly once across $D$ blindfolding rounds.
2. Iterative Re-estimation: For each round, the omitted data points are treated as missing; model parameters (weights, loadings, path coefficients) are estimated on the remaining observations.
3. Prediction Imputation: Omitted data points are predicted using the estimated structural equations and indicator loading matrices.
4. Calculation of $Q^2$:
$$Q^2 = 1 - \frac{\sum_j \text{SSE}_j}{\sum_j \text{SSO}_j}$$
where $\text{SSE}_j$ is the sum of squared prediction errors for indicator $j$, and $\text{SSO}_j$ is the sum of squared errors using the trivial mean as the predictor.
5. Construct Cross-Validation: Evaluated separately for each endogenous reflective construct in the structural model.
terms.benchmarks:
Established empirical benchmarks (Hair et al., 2019; Sarstedt et al., 2017):
- Baseline Threshold: $Q^2 > 0$ confirms the model has predictive relevance; $Q^2 \le 0$ indicates lack of predictive relevance.
- Relative Effect Sizing ($q^2$): Measures the relative impact of an exogenous construct on an endogenous construct's $Q^2$:
$$q^2 = \frac{Q^2_{\text{included}} - Q^2_{\text{excluded}}}{1 - Q^2_{\text{included}}}$$
Benchmarks: $q^2 \approx 0.02$ (Small), $q^2 \approx 0.15$ (Medium), $q^2 \approx 0.35$ (Large).
- Out-of-Sample PLSpredict Comparison: $Q^2$ should be reported alongside Shmueli et al.'s (2019) $Q^2_{\text{predict}}$ benchmarked against a naive linear model (LM).
terms.pitfalls:
Common research design errors in PLS manuscripts:
1. Reporting Blindfolding on Single-Item Constructs: Computing $Q^2$ on single-item endogenous constructs, where blindfolding collapses into a trivial arithmetic tautology.
2. Omitting the Omission Distance Value: Failing to report the specific omission distance $D$ used in SmartPLS or ADANCO, reducing audit transparency.
3. Equating $Q^2$ with Pure Machine Learning Out-of-Sample Prediction: Confusing blindfolding $Q^2$ with genuine out-of-sample holdout test set cross-validation ($Q^2_{\text{predict}}$), which is a much stricter test of predictive power.
terms.apa_reference: Hair, J. F., Hult, G. T. M., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2017). A primer on partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) (2nd ed.). SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Xác minh chéo trong dữ liệu định tính
terms.core_definition: Cross-Verification in Qualitative Data—integrating Norman K. Denzin's (1978) classic triangulation typology with Yvonna S. Lincoln and Egon G. Guba's (1985) naturalistic trustworthiness criteria—is an active qualitative validation procedure wherein findings, factual claims, and thematic assertions are systematically verified by contrasting data obtained across different informants, independent data collection methods, distinct physical observation sites, and temporal moments. By testing whether a phenomenon holds true across diverse observational vantage points, cross-verification eliminates idiosyncratic informant bias, detects deception, and establishes empirical credibility.
terms.seminal_citation: Denzin, N. K. (1978). The research act: A theoretical introduction to sociological methods (2nd ed.). McGraw-Hill.
terms.expert_notes: Đã được biên tập và chuẩn hóa định nghĩa học thuật theo giáo trình kinh điển.
terms.core_definition_en: Rigorous scholarly definition of Cross-verification according to established research methodology literature.
terms.operational_mechanism:
Cross-verification operates through four systematic verification matrices:
1. Informant-to-Informant Cross-Verification: Comparing the testimony of frontline operational employees against middle managers, top executives, and outside customers regarding the exact same organizational event.
2. Method-to-Method Cross-Verification: Juxtaposing interview statements with formal archival documents, internal emails, and firsthand field observations (e.g., verifying whether managers who claim 'we have an open-door policy' actually exhibit open-door behaviors during unobtrusive observation).
3. Temporal and Spatial Cross-Verification: Observing whether behaviors recorded during daylight public shifts are consistent with night shifts or informal backstage settings.
4. Discrepancy Auditing: When cross-verification reveals contradictions, the researcher does not discard the discrepancy, but investigates the sociological reason for the mismatch (e.g., impression management, power asymmetry, or conflicting subcultures).
terms.benchmarks:
Trustworthiness benchmarks (Lincoln & Guba, 1985; Patton, 2015):
- Multiple Data Source Requirement: No substantive factual finding or critical incident should rely on a single isolated interview statement unless corroborated by documentary or observational evidence.
- Cross-Verification Audit Trail: Methodological supplementary materials should document an explicit data-source matrix showing how key findings were cross-verified.
- Truthfulness in Contradiction: Demonstrating that discrepancies are treated as valuable analytical insights rather than suppressed.
terms.pitfalls:
Common qualitative weaknesses in journal submissions:
1. Single-Source Vulnerability: Building an entire qualitative case study around the charismatic, polished narrative of a single CEO without cross-verifying with frontline staff or union representatives.
2. Superficial Triangulation: Claiming cross-verification simply because two interviews were conducted, without utilizing distinct methods or diverse stakeholder perspectives.
3. Sweeping Contradictions Under the Rug: Forcing disparate findings into an artificial narrative of complete consensus, ignoring institutional tensions.
terms.apa_reference: Lincoln, Y. S., & Guba, E. G. (1985). Naturalistic inquiry. SAGE Publications.

terms.term: CRSP Database (Center for Research in Security Prices)
terms.vietnamese: Cơ sở dữ liệu chứng khoán CRSP (Đại học Chicago)
vietnamese_variants: Cơ sở dữ liệu chứng khoán CRSP qua WRDS
terms.core_definition: The CRSP Database (Center for Research in Security Prices)—founded at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business by Lawrence Fisher and James H. Lorie in 1960—is the world's most authoritative, comprehensive, and survivorship-bias-free historical stock market database for US equities. Distributed via Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS), CRSP provides standardized daily and monthly security prices, returns, trading volumes, dividends, and shares outstanding for all publicly traded stocks on the NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ exchanges dating back to December 1926, serving as the empirical foundation for modern empirical asset pricing, event studies, and market efficiency tests.
terms.seminal_citation: Fisher, L., & Lorie, J. H. (1964). Rates of return on investments in common stocks. The Journal of Business, 37(1), 1-21. https://doi.org/10.1086/294657
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of CRSP Database (Center for Research in Security Prices) according to Fisher & Lorie (1964).
terms.operational_mechanism:
Archival data extraction and processing follow four rigorous econometric protocols:
1. Permanent Identifier Utilization: Tracking firms using the permanent security identifier `PERMNO` and company identifier `PERMCO`, rather than ticker symbols or CUSIPs which change frequently over corporate history.
2. Survivorship Bias Elimination: Tracking active and delisted firms; incorporating CRSP delisting codes (`DLSTCD`) and delisting returns (`DLRET`) to accurately capture terminal losses (e.g., bankruptcy or mergers).
3. Dividend and Split Adjustment: Using raw returns (`RET`) which incorporate total returns including reinvested cash dividends, and adjustment factors (`CFACPR` and `CFACSHR`) to adjust historical prices and share counts for stock splits.
4. Merging with Compustat (CCM): Linking CRSP equity trading data with Compustat accounting balance sheet data via the official CRSP/Compustat Merged (CCM) Link Table using `GVKEY` and `PERMNO` with link type `LU` and link priority `P`.
terms.benchmarks:
Empirical finance standards (Fisher & Lorie, 1964; Fama & French, 1992, 1993):
- Delisting Return Correction: Failure to include delisting returns (`DLRET`) introduces massive positive survivorship bias; when `DLRET` is missing for bankruptcy delistings (codes 500–591), standard empirical practice applies a $-30\%$ or $-100\%$ terminal return penalty (Shumway, 1997).
- Market Factor Construction: CRSP value-weighted market return (`VWRETD`) serves as the standard market proxy in CAPM and Fama-French factor regressions.
- Event Study Baseline: Daily CRSP returns provide the benchmark estimation windows (typically $[-250, -21]$ trading days) for estimating market model parameters prior to corporate events.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research blunders in financial economics submissions:
1. Ignoring Delisting Returns: Calculating buy-and-hold returns by dropping firms when they delist, which systematically discards catastrophic bankruptcy drops and inflates portfolio returns.
2. Ticker-Based Merging: Merging external datasets with CRSP using stock tickers, linking modern firms to unrelated historical entities that previously held the same ticker.
3. Conflating Ordinary Shares with Incommensurate Securities: Failing to filter by share code (`SHRCD` 10 or 11 for US ordinary common shares), inadvertently including ADRs, REITs, closed-end funds, and foreign trusts.
terms.apa_reference: Wharton Research Data Services. (2022). CRSP data description guide. The Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania.

Phổ phương pháp khảo sát định lượng
terms.core_definition: The Quantitative Survey Continuum—conceptualized within survey methodology by Robert M. Groves et al. (2009) and Don A. Dillman et al. (2014)—is a theoretical and operational spectrum that spans from purely descriptive, standardized cross-sectional polling to complex, longitudinal panel tracking and experimental survey designs. Grounded in the Total Survey Error (TSE) framework, the continuum structures the trade-offs between measurement precision, sampling error, coverage error, non-response bias, and cognitive respondent burden across different survey administration modes (web, mail, telephone, and face-to-face).
terms.seminal_citation: Groves, R. M., Fowler, F. J., Couper, M. P., Lepkowski, J. M., Singer, E., & Tourangeau, R. (2009). Survey methodology (2nd ed.). John Wiley & Sons.
terms.expert_notes: Tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cực Định lượng & Khảo sát according to Silverman (2016).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The continuum structures survey research across four operational pillars:
1. Total Survey Error (TSE) Decomposition:
   - Measurement Track: Construct $\to$ Measurement $\to$ Response $\to$ Edited Response.
   - Representation Track: Target Population $\to$ Sampling Frame $\to$ Sample $\to$ Respondents $\to$ Post-stratification Weighting.
2. Survey Mode Selection Continuum:
   - Self-Administered Web/Mail: Minimal interviewer bias and low cost, but vulnerable to coverage error and low response rates.
   - Interviewer-Administered Phone/In-Person: High response rates and probe capabilities, but vulnerable to social desirability and high interviewer variance.
3. Mixed-Mode Design: Sequencing survey modes (e.g., Web-push design followed by mail or phone follow-up) to optimize sample coverage.
4. Non-Response Bias Auditing: Comparing early vs. late respondents (Armstrong & Overton, 1977) and benchmarking sample demographics against national census parameters.
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological standards (Groves et al., 2009; Dillman et al., 2014):
- Response Rate Benchmarking: Reporting AAPOR (American Association for Public Opinion Research) standardized response rate formulas (RR1 through RR6).
- Non-Response Bias Testing: Formal statistical comparison of respondent demographics against non-respondents or population census baselines.
- Questionnaire Pretesting: Mandatory cognitive pretesting or pilot testing prior to full-scale survey launch.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research weaknesses in survey-based papers:
1. Concealing the Response Rate: Reporting only the final sample size ($N = 400$) without disclosing the sampling frame, total invitations sent, or response rate.
2. Relying on Unadjusted Convenience Panels: Using low-cost crowdsourced samples (e.g., generic MTurk or social media clicks) without post-stratification weighting or attention-check filters, yielding low data quality.
3. Common Method Bias: Measuring all independent and dependent variables through a single survey instrument without procedural separation.
terms.apa_reference: Dillman, D. A., Smyth, J. D., & Christian, L. M. (2014). Internet, phone, mail, and mixed-mode surveys: The tailored design method (4th ed.). John Wiley & Sons.

terms.vietnamese: Cực định tính thực địa (Phổ phương pháp thực địa định tính)
vietnamese_variants: Phổ nghiên cứu thực địa định tính
terms.core_definition: The Qualitative Fieldwork Continuum—conceptualized by John Van Maanen (1988, 2011) and Michael Agar (1996)—is a methodological and epistemological spectrum capturing the varied degrees of researcher immersion, participation, and textual representation in ethnographic and qualitative fieldwork. Spanning from complete detached observation (the fly-on-the-wall stance) to full participant immersion (indigenous ethnography and 'going native'), the continuum structures how researchers negotiate physical entry, relational trust, ethical boundaries, cognitive access, and ethnographic authority when studying social groups in their natural habitats.
terms.seminal_citation: Van Maanen, J. (1988). Tales of the field: On writing ethnography. University of Chicago Press.
terms.expert_notes: Tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cực Định tính & Thực địa according to Silverman (2016).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The continuum structures fieldwork across four participant-observer roles (Gold, 1958; Van Maanen, 1988):
1. Complete Observer: Completely detached, non-intrusive observation without interaction; high observational discretion, but zero cognitive access to internal participant mental models.
2. Observer-as-Participant: Research role is public and known, with brief, formal interview interactions during site visits.
3. Participant-as-Observer: The researcher actively participates in daily workplace or communal tasks alongside informants while openly acknowledging their research role, developing deep empathetic rapport.
4. Complete Participant: Full immersion where the researcher becomes an authentic insider (covert or organic), gaining total access to backstage realities at the risk of losing analytical detachment.
5. Van Maanen's Ethnographic Tales:
   - Realist Tales: Direct, unmediated reporting of participant worlds in an authoritative, third-person voice.
   - Confessional Tales: Highly personalized accounts exposing fieldwork errors, self-doubt, and vulnerabilities.
   - Impressionist Tales: Vivid, dramatic storytelling capturing intense, memorable field moments.
terms.benchmarks:
Ethnographic quality criteria (Van Maanen, 2011; Spradley, 1979):
- Prolonged Immersion: Fieldwork must involve substantial temporal immersion (months or years) to move past front-stage public relations performances into backstage cultural truths.
- Thick Description: Field notes must capture sensory details, verbatim speech idioms, spatial layouts, and emotional micro-climates.
- Reflexive Accountability: The researcher must transparently document how their physical presence and social identities altered the field dynamics.
terms.pitfalls:
Common fieldwork hazards in qualitative papers:
1. The 'Drive-By' Ethnography: Spending three days at an organization and claiming to have conducted an 'in-depth ethnography', resulting in superficial, descriptive cliches.
2. Uncritical Going Native: Becoming so emotionally enmeshed in the host culture that the researcher adopts the participants' rationalizations uncritically, losing scholarly analytical detachment.
3. Ethical Betrayal: Publishing sensitive backstage organizational secrets or participant vulnerabilities without rigorous anonymization and informed consent.
terms.apa_reference: Van Maanen, J. (2011). Ethnography as work, career, and commitment. In Tales of the field: On writing ethnography (2nd ed., pp. 147-172). University of Chicago Press.

terms.vietnamese: Lợi nhuận bất thường lũy kế (CAR)
vietnamese_variants: Tỷ suất sinh lợi bất thường tích lũy
Chỉ số CAR trong Event Study
terms.core_definition: Cumulative Abnormal Return (CAR) is the central metric in financial event study methodology, originated by Eugene F. Fama, Lawrence Fisher, Michael C. Jensen, and Richard Roll (1969) and formalized by A. Craig MacKinlay (1997). In corporate finance and empirical accounting, CAR measures the total excess stock return earned by a firm over a specified multi-day event window surrounding a corporate announcement (e.g., M&A, earnings surprises, CEO dismissal, ESG scandals), beyond the normal return predicted by asset pricing models (e.g., Market Model, CAPM, or Fama-French factor models). By aggregating abnormal returns over time, CAR captures the net market valuation impact of new information under the Efficient Market Hypothesis.
terms.seminal_citation: Fama, E. F., Fisher, L., Jensen, M. C., & Roll, R. (1969). The adjustment of stock prices to new information. International Economic Review, 10(1), 1-21. https://doi.org/10.2307/2525569
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cumulative Abnormal Return (CAR) according to MacKinlay (1997).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The econometric calculation unfolds across four sequential steps:
1. Normal Return Estimation Window: Estimate the parameters of the Market Model over an estimation window prior to the event (typically $t = -250$ to $t = -21$ trading days):
$$R_{it} = \alpha_i + \beta_i R_{mt} + \epsilon_{it}$$
where $R_{it}$ is firm stock return, $R_{mt}$ is CRSP value-weighted market return, and $\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{it}] = 0$.
2. Abnormal Return Computation: For each day $t$ in the event window (e.g., $t \in [t_1, t_2]$, such as $[-1, +1]$ days surrounding announcement day $0$):
$$\text{AR}_{it} = R_{it} - \left( \hat{\alpha}_i + \hat{\beta}_i R_{mt} \right)$$
3. Cumulative Abnormal Return (CAR): Sum the abnormal returns across the event window:
$$\text{CAR}_i(t_1, t_2) = \sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \text{AR}_{it}$$
4. Cumulative Average Abnormal Return (CAAR) & Hypothesis Testing: Average CARs across $N$ sample firms: $\text{CAAR} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \text{CAR}_i$. Statistical significance is tested using the Patell $z$-test, Boehmer-Musumeci-Poulsen (BMP) standardized test, or the non-parametric Corrado rank test to adjust for event-induced variance.
terms.benchmarks:
Established empirical benchmarks (MacKinlay, 1997; Kothari & Warner, 2007):
- Short Event Windows: Short windows (e.g., $[-1, +1]$ or $[0, +1]$ days) are the gold standard; short windows maximize statistical power and are immune to asset pricing model misspecification.
- Long-Horizon Warning: For long event windows (1 to 3 years), Buy-and-Hold Abnormal Returns (BHAR) must be used instead of CAR, because CAR suffers from severe compounding bias and rebalancing artifacts over extended periods.
- Event-Induced Volatility: Must report BMP standardized residual tests or Cowan generalized sign tests to control for event-induced volatility clustering.
terms.pitfalls:
Common econometric errors in finance submissions:
1. Event Window Contamination: Using an excessively wide event window (e.g., $[-30, +30]$ days), allowing confounding corporate news (earnings releases, macro announcements) to contaminate the focal event.
2. Compounding CAR Over Long Horizons: Summing daily returns over 3 years to calculate CAR; summing daily returns assumes continuous daily portfolio rebalancing with zero transaction costs, severely overstating long-term performance (BHAR is required).
3. Cross-Sectional Correlation (Event Clustering): Applying standard $t$-tests when multiple sample firms experience the event on the exact same calendar date (e.g., industry-wide regulatory shock), which causes severe standard error deflation (requires Jaffe-Mandelker clustering adjustments).
terms.apa_reference: MacKinlay, A. C. (1997). Event studies in economics and finance. Journal of Economic Literature, 35(1), 13-39.

terms.term: Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) and CUSUMSQ Stability Tests
terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định độ ổn định tham số CUSUM và CUSUMSQ
vietnamese_variants: Kiểm định tổng tích lũy phần dư hồi quy
terms.core_definition: Kiểm định CUSUM và CUSUMSQ (Brown, Durbin, & Evans, 1975) là các phép kiểm định đồ thị chẩn đoán độ ổn định của các hệ số hồi quy theo thời gian. Dựa trên tổng tích lũy của các phần dư đệ quy (recursive residuals), kiểm định giúp phát hiện xem các hệ số của mô hình có bị thay đổi đột ngột hoặc trôi dạt dần dần (gradual parameter drift) trong suốt thời kỳ nghiên cứu hay không.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cumulative Sum Control Chart Test according to Đường biểu diễn CUSUM và CUSUMSQ phải nằm hoàn toàn bên trong hai dải biên tới hạn ở mức ý nghĩa 5%..
terms.benchmarks: Độ ổn định mô hình được xác nhận khi và chỉ khi toàn bộ đường biểu diễn của thống kê CUSUM và CUSUMSQ nằm hoàn toàn bên trong hai đường biên giới hạn 5%. Nếu đường CUSUM hoặc CUSUMSQ cắt ra ngoài biên tại bất kỳ thời điểm nào, mô hình bị vi phạm tính ổn định cấu trúc tại vùng thời gian đó.
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Ước lượng các phương trình hồi quy đệ quy tăng dần từ kích thước mẫu k đến T, trích xuất chuỗi phần dư đệ quy chuẩn hóa w_t. 2. CUSUM: Tổng tích lũy W_t = sum_{j=k+1}^t w_j / sigma_hat. Giúp phát hiện sự thay đổi có tính hệ thống trong các hệ số hồi quy beta. 3. CUSUMSQ: Tổng tích lũy bình phương S_t = sum w_j^2 / sum w_i^2. Giúp phát hiện sự bất ổn định đột ngột trong phương sai của sai số ngẫu nhiên. 4. Thiết lập hai đường biên tới hạn (critical boundary lines) ở mức ý nghĩa 5%.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Bỏ qua việc báo cáo đồ thị CUSUM/CUSUMSQ khi công bố mô hình ARDL hoặc VAR. Nếu đường CUSUM vượt ra ngoài dải biên giới hạn, các kết luận phân tích tác động dài hạn và ngắn hạn sẽ không có giá trị suy diễn đáng tin cậy do mô hình đã bị thay đổi cấu trúc mà không được kiểm soát.
terms.apa_reference: Brown, R. L., Durbin, J., & Evans, J. M. (1975). Techniques for testing the constancy of regression relationships over time. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 37(2), 149–163. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1975.tb01532.x

terms.vietnamese: Mô hình hồi quy phi tuyến đường cong (Hiệu ứng bậc hai)
vietnamese_variants: Quan hệ chữ U và chữ U ngược
terms.core_definition: Mô hình hồi quy đường cong (Curvilinear Regression) mô hình hóa mối quan hệ phi tuyến dạng bậc hai giữa biến giải thích X và biến kết quả Y (y = beta_0 + beta_1*X + beta_2*X^2 + e), thường được dùng để kiểm định các giả thuyết lý thuyết về quan hệ chữ U ngược (Inverted U-shaped: lợi ích ban đầu tăng dần nhưng sau ngưỡng tối ưu sẽ phản tác dụng, 'too-much-of-a-good-thing effect') hoặc chữ U thuận.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Curvilinear Regression Modeling according to Aiken & West (1991).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Chuẩn hóa định tâm biến X trước khi bình phương (Mean-centering X: x_c = X - mean(X)) để giảm thiểu hiện tượng đa cộng tuyến không bản chất giữa bậc 1 và bậc 2. 2. Ước lượng hồi quy OLS bậc hai. 3. Xác định điểm cực trị (inflection point / turning point): X* = -beta_1 / (2 * beta_2). 4. Kiểm định ba bước Lind & Mehlum (2010 - U-test): Bắt buộc kiểm tra độ dốc ở cả hai đầu mút của miền giá trị quan sát.
terms.benchmarks: Quy chuẩn Lind & Mehlum (2010): Để khẳng định quan hệ chữ U ngược có hiệu lực thực sự: (1) beta_2 phải âm và có ý nghĩa thống kê (p < 0.05); (2) Độ dốc ở giá trị nhỏ nhất của X phải dương có ý nghĩa (slope_min > 0); (3) Độ dốc ở giá trị lớn nhất của X phải âm có ý nghĩa (slope_max < 0); (4) Điểm cực trị X* phải nằm hoàn toàn bên trong khoảng giá trị thực tế của dữ liệu kèm khoảng tin cậy Fieller 95%.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện kinh điển: Chỉ dựa vào hệ số beta_2 có ý nghĩa thống kê để tuyên bố quan hệ chữ U ngược mà không kiểm định U-test. Rất nhiều trường hợp điểm cực trị X* nằm ngoài phạm vi mẫu thực tế, khiến cho mối quan hệ thực chất chỉ là hàm lồi/lõm đơn điệu chứ không phải chữ U hoàn chỉnh.
terms.apa_reference: Lind, J. T., & Mehlum, H. (2010). With or without U? The appropriate test for a U-shaped relationship. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 72(1), 109–118. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0084.2009.00569.x

terms.vietnamese: Biểu đồ kiểm soát tổng tích lũy (CUSUM)
vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật kiểm soát chất lượng CUSUM
Cumulative Sum Chart in Quality Control
terms.core_definition: The Cumulative Sum Control Chart (CUSUM)—invented by E. S. Page (1954) and modernized by Douglas M. Hawkins and David H. Olwell (1998)—is a sequential statistical analysis technique and control chart used to detect small, persistent shifts in the mean or variance of a stochastic process over time. In econometrics and time-series modeling (Brown, Durbin, & Evans, 1975), the CUSUM and CUSUM-squared tests are foundational diagnostic tests applied to recursive OLS regression residuals to assess structural parameter stability and detect structural breaks at unknown change-points.
terms.seminal_citation: Page, E. S. (1954). Continuous inspection schemes. Biometrika, 41(1/2), 100-115. https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/41.1-2.100
terms.expert_notes: Nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of CUSUM according to Đường biểu diễn CUSUM và CUSUMSQ phải nằm hoàn toàn bên trong hai dải biên tới hạn ở mức ý nghĩa 5%..
terms.operational_mechanism:
The mathematical formulation operates across two primary domains:
1. Statistical Process Control (Page, 1954):
   - Tabular Two-Sided CUSUM: For standardized observations $z_t = (x_t - \mu_0) / \sigma$ and reference allowance parameter $k$:
$$C_t^+ = \max\left(0, \; C_{t-1}^+ + z_t - k\right)$$
$$C_t^- = \max\left(0, \; C_{t-1}^- - z_t - k\right)$$
An out-of-control signal is triggered if either $C_t^+$ or $C_t^-$ exceeds decision boundary threshold $h$.
2. Econometric Structural Stability Test (Brown, Durbin, & Evans, 1975):
   - Recursive Residuals ($w_t$): Compute standardized one-step-ahead forecast errors from recursive OLS regressions from $t = k+1$ to $T$.
   - CUSUM Test Statistic:
$$W_t = \sum_{r=k+1}^t \frac{w_r}{\hat{\sigma}_w}$$
   - Decision Boundary: Plotted against critical boundary lines $c \pm a(t - k)$; if $W_t$ crosses the critical boundaries at significance level $\alpha$ (typically 5%), the null hypothesis of parameter constancy is rejected, proving a structural break occurred.
   - CUSUM-of-Squares ($S_t$): Evaluates stability of residual variance over time.
terms.benchmarks:
Established empirical benchmarks (Page, 1954; Brown et al., 1975; Hawkins & Olwell, 1998):
- Superiority Over Shewhart Charts: CUSUM detects small shifts (0.5 to 1.5 standard deviations) much faster than standard Shewhart charts because it accumulates historical evidence across successive observations.
- Econometric Diagnostic Standard: High-impact macro-econometric and ARDL papers universally report CUSUM and CUSUM-squared plots to confirm that cointegrating regression parameters remain stable across decades.
- Average Run Length (ARL): Calibrated via parameters $(k, h)$ such that in-control $\text{ARL}_0$ is large (e.g., 500 samples before a false alarm) while out-of-control $\text{ARL}_1$ is small.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research misinterpretations:
1. Neglecting Autocorrelation in Process Control: Running standard CUSUM on serially correlated time series without modeling the underlying ARMA process; positive autocorrelation drastically reduces in-control ARL, triggering rampant false-positive alarms.
2. Over-Interpreting Small Boundary Crossings: Treating a momentary, tiny boundary touch in econometric CUSUM as definitive proof of regime change without conducting Chow or Bai-Perron multiple breakpoint tests.
3. Confusing CUSUM with CUSUM-Squared: CUSUM tests for structural breaks in the regression slope coefficients (mean shifts); CUSUM-squared tests for heteroskedasticity or structural shifts in residual variance.
terms.apa_reference: Brown, R. L., Durbin, J., & Evans, J. M. (1975). Techniques for testing the constancy of regression relationships over time. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 37(2), 149-163. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1975.tb01532.x

terms.vietnamese: Khái niệm tách biệt định hướng (d-Separation)
vietnamese_variants: Tính tách biệt định hướng d-separation
Tiêu chuẩn d-separation của Judea Pearl
terms.core_definition: d-Separation (Directional Separation) is the foundational graph-theoretic criterion in causal inference, probabilistic graphical models, and Bayesian networks, formulated by Judea Pearl (1988, 2000, 2009). d-Separation provides a complete, sound mathematical algorithm that reads conditional independence relations directly from the topology of a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). If a set of conditioning nodes $Z$ d-separates variable $X$ from variable $Y$ in a DAG, then $X$ and $Y$ are guaranteed to be statistically independent conditional on $Z$ ($X \perp Y \mid Z$) across all probability distributions compatible with that graph.
terms.seminal_citation: Pearl, J. (1988). Probabilistic reasoning in intelligent systems: Networks of plausible inference. Morgan Kaufmann Publishers.
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of d-separation according to Kline (2023); Kline (2023).
terms.operational_mechanism:
d-Separation evaluates whether a path between $X$ and $Y$ is blocked by conditioning set $Z$ based on three fundamental causal junctions:
1. Chain Junction ($X \to M \to Y$): Conditioning on the intermediate node $M$ blocks the path ($X \perp Y \mid M$). Unconditioned, the path is open.
2. Fork Junction ($X \leftarrow C \to Y$): Common cause (confounder). Conditioning on the common cause $C$ blocks the path ($X \perp Y \mid C$). Unconditioned, the path is open.
3. Collider Junction ($X \to K \leftarrow Y$): Common effect. A collider is naturally BLOCKED when unconditioned ($X \perp Y$). Crucially, conditioning on the collider $K$ (or any descendant of $K$) *OPENS* the path, inducing a spurious correlation between $X$ and $Y$ (collider stratification bias / Berkson's paradox).
4. Formal d-Separation Theorem: A path is d-separated (blocked) by set $Z$ if and only if:
   - The path contains a chain ($A \to B \to C$) or fork ($A \leftarrow B \to C$) such that the middle node $B$ is in $Z$, OR
   - The path contains a collider ($A \to B \leftarrow C$) such that neither the middle node $B$ nor any descendant of $B$ is in $Z$.
5. Global d-Separation: $X$ and $Y$ are d-separated by $Z$ if and only if *every* path between $X$ and $Y$ is blocked by $Z$.
terms.benchmarks:
Causal inference standards (Pearl, 2009; Elwert, 2013):
- Backdoor Criterion Foundation: Pearl's famous Backdoor Criterion is a direct special case of d-separation applied to non-causal paths entering treatment $X$.
- Testable Implications (Vanishing Tetrads): d-Separation identifies non-causal conditional independencies that allow empirical researchers to test whether a hypothesized DAG is falsified by empirical sample data.
- Minimally Sufficient Adjustment Sets: Algorithmic identification of the smallest set of variables that blocks all non-causal paths without opening collider paths (readily computed via DAGitty or `ggdag` in R).
terms.pitfalls:
Common causal modeling blunders in empirical papers:
1. The Collider Conditioning Trap (M-Bias): Conditioning on a variable without realizing it is a collider ($A \to C \leftarrow B$), thereby opening a spurious association and creating artificial confounding.
2. Overcontrolling on Mediators: Conditioning on a node that lies on a chain path ($X \to M \to Y$), accidentally blocking the very causal mechanism being studied.
3. Assuming Causal Directionality from Correlation Alone: Forgetting that multiple distinct DAGs can share identical d-separation properties (Markov Equivalence Class); observational data alone cannot distinguish between DAGs within the same equivalence class without experimental interventions or temporal ordering.
terms.apa_reference: Pearl, J. (2009). Causality: Models, reasoning, and inference (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511803161

terms.vietnamese: Đánh giá giá trị nội dung thực nghiệm (Quy trình Hinkin & MacKenzie)
vietnamese_variants: Thẩm định hiệu lực nội dung thực nghiệm
Quy trình đánh giá nội dung Hinkin
terms.core_definition: Empirical Content Validity Assessment refers to the structured, quantitative methodological protocols formulated by Timothy R. Hinkin (1995, 1998) and Scott B. MacKenzie, Philip M. Podsakoff, and Nathan P. Podsakoff (2011) that elevate traditional subjective content validation into a statistically testable empirical stage of scale development. Rather than relying solely on informal expert opinions, empirical content validity uses sorting tasks, item-construct substantive agreement coefficients, and analysis of variance (ANOVA) on independent pretest panels to mathematically verify that items belong uniquely to their designated construct domain before full-scale survey deployment.
terms.seminal_citation: Hinkin, T. R. (1995). A review of scale development practices in the study of organizations. Journal of Management, 21(5), 967-988. https://doi.org/10.1177/014920639502100509
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Đánh giá Giá trị Nội dung Thực nghiệm according to MacKenzie et al. (2011).
terms.operational_mechanism:
Hinkin and MacKenzie's empirical validation protocol executes four procedural steps:
1. Item Sorting Task (Card-Sorting / Matrix Sorting): An independent panel of respondents (typically 50–100 educated pretest participants or graduate students) is presented with the randomized list of candidate items alongside explicit conceptual definitions of the target construct and adjacent rival constructs.
2. Substantive Validity Coefficient ($c_{sa}$):
$$c_{sa} = \frac{n_c - n_o}{N}$$
where $n_c$ is the number of respondents assigning the item to its hypothesized construct, $n_o$ is the highest number of assignments to any alternative construct, and $N$ is total panel size. Ranging from $-1.0$ to $+1.0$, $c_{sa}$ evaluates whether assignment to the correct construct exceeds chance.
3. Proportion of Substantive Agreement ($p_{sa}$):
$$p_{sa} = \frac{n_c}{N}$$
Measures the percentage of respondents correctly matching the item to its theoretical definition.
4. Within-Subjects ANOVA Testing: Rating tasks where experts rate the extent to which each item reflects multiple constructs on 5-point scales; repeated-measures ANOVA tests whether an item's rating on its intended construct is significantly higher ($p < 0.01$) than on competing constructs.
terms.benchmarks:
Scale development benchmarks (Hinkin, 1998; MacKenzie et al., 2011):
- Substantive Agreement Cutoff: Items should achieve $p_{sa} \ge 0.75$ (at least 75% of panelists correctly categorize the item) and $c_{sa} \ge 0.50$ (statistically significant at $p < 0.05$ via binomial testing).
- Elimination of Contaminated Items: Any item that exhibits high assignment ($> 20\%$) to a rival construct is flagged as contaminated and deleted immediately.
- Mandatory Pre-CFA Phase: This quantitative pre-testing must be executed *prior* to collecting large-sample data for Exploratory or Confirmatory Factor Analysis.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research weaknesses in scale development:
1. Skipping Empirical Pre-Testing: Relying entirely on the author's own intuition that items 'look right', resulting in catastrophic factor cross-loadings during subsequent CFA.
2. Using Biased Judges: Asking the original scale authors or their direct research assistants to complete the sorting task, completely compromising objectivity.
3. Omitting Rival Construct Definitions: Providing panelists with only the target construct definition, making it impossible to detect item overlap with adjacent concepts in the nomological network.
terms.apa_reference: MacKenzie, S. B., Podsakoff, P. M., & Podsakoff, N. P. (2011). Construct measurement and validation procedures in MIS and behavioral research: Integrating new and existing techniques. MIS Quarterly, 35(2), 293-334. https://doi.org/10.2307/23044045

terms.vietnamese: Bộ ba tính cách đen tối (Dark Triad)
vietnamese_variants: Bộ ba bóng tối tính cách
Thuyết Dark Triad trong tâm lý học
terms.core_definition: The Dark Triad of Personality is a prominent psychometric and behavioral framework, conceptualized by Delroy L. Paulhus and Kevin M. Williams (2002) and standardized by Peter K. Jonason and Gregory D. Webster (2010; Dirty Dozen scale) and Daniel N. Jones and Delroy L. Paulhus (2014; Short Dark Triad - SD3). The framework delineates three distinct yet overlapping, socially aversive, and subclinical personality dimensions: (1) Machiavellianism (strategic manipulation, cynical amorality, and long-term deceit), (2) Subclinical Narcissism (grandiosity, entitlement, exhibitionism, and ego-defensiveness), and (3) Subclinical Psychopathy (high impulsivity, thrill-seeking, callousness, and profound lack of empathy).
terms.seminal_citation: Paulhus, D. L., & Williams, K. M. (2002). The dark triad of personality: Narcissism, Machiavellianism, and psychopathy. Journal of Research in Personality, 36(6), 556-563. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0092-6566(02)00505-6
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Dark Triad Personality Traits according to Paulhus & Williams (2002).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The psychometric measurement and operational profile unfold as follows:
1. Three Factor Dimensions:
   - Machiavellianism (High Mach): Strategic, patient calculation; instrumental social relationships; cold, goal-oriented deceit (measured via Christie & Geis's Mach-IV or SD3).
   - Narcissism: Preoccupation with status, superiority, vanity, and hypersensitivity to perceived disrespect (measured via NPI-16 or SD3).
   - Psychopathy: Immediate gratification, reckless risk-taking, low impulse control, and ruthless indifference to the suffering of others (measured via SRP-III or SD3).
2. Standardized Measurement Instruments:
   - Dirty Dozen (Jonason & Webster, 2010): 12-item concise screening scale (4 items per trait).
   - Short Dark Triad (SD3; Jones & Paulhus, 2014): 27-item validated scale (9 items per trait) providing superior construct breadth.
3. Common Core vs. Unique Facets: The three traits share a common antagonistic core of low Agreeableness (HEXACO Honesty-Humility deficiency), yet exhibit distinct structural relationships with workplace counterproductive work behaviors (CWB), white-collar financial fraud, and ethical violations.
terms.benchmarks:
Empirical and psychometric benchmarks (Paulhus & Williams, 2002; Jones & Paulhus, 2014):
- Subclinical Spectrum: Must be operationalized as continuous personality traits in normal non-institutionalized populations, NOT as psychiatric DSM clinical diagnoses.
- Discriminant Factor Validity: Confirmatory factor analysis must demonstrate that a 3-factor model fits significantly better than a single general 'darkness' factor (inter-factor correlations typically range between $r = 0.30$ and $0.50$).
- Common Method Bias Controls: Because dark traits involve socially undesirable behaviors, self-reports should ideally be paired with other-reports (peer, subordinate ratings) or objective behavioral tracking.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research flaws in management and psychology submissions:
1. Conflating Subclinical Traits with Clinical Pathology: Using the term 'psychopath' or 'narcissist' as clinical diagnostic labels in organizational studies, ignoring that the scales measure normal-range personality variations.
2. Summing All Traits into an Unweighted Aggregate: Combining Machiavellianism, Narcissism, and Psychopathy into a single composite score, obscuring that the traits frequently predict opposite organizational outcomes (e.g., Machs are highly self-controlled; psychopaths are highly impulsive).
3. Social Desirability Denial: Administering self-report dark trait scales in high-stakes job hiring contexts without social desirability controls, where applicants easily fake desirable answers.
terms.apa_reference: Jones, D. N., & Paulhus, D. L. (2014). Introducing the Short Dark Triad (SD3): A brief measure of dark personality traits. Assessment, 21(1), 28-41. https://doi.org/10.1177/1073191113514105

terms.vietnamese: Dasein (Hiện hữu trong thế giới / Hiện hữu thực tại)
terms.core_definition: Dasein (literally 'being-there' or 'existence') is the foundational existential and ontological concept formulated by German philosopher Martin Heidegger (1927) in 'Being and Time' (Sein und Zeit), serving as the philosophical bedrock for Hermeneutic (Interpretive) Phenomenology (Max van Manen, 2014; Jonathan Smith's Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis - IPA). Rejecting the Cartesian mind-body dualism and Husserl's transcendental ego (which assumes a detached consciousness observing an external world), Dasein defines human existence as fundamentally and indivisibly 'Being-in-the-World' (In-der-Welt-sein)—meaning human beings are always already embedded, situated, and engaged in a pre-reflective, historical, linguistic, and cultural context.
terms.seminal_citation: Heidegger, M. (1927). Sein und Zeit [Being and time]. Max Niemeyer Verlag.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Dasein (Being-in-the-World) according to Heidegger (1927).
terms.operational_mechanism:
Heidegger's existential analytic transforms qualitative research across four core dimensions:
1. Rejection of the Husserlian 'Epoché' (Bracketing): In descriptive phenomenology, Husserl argued researchers must 'bracket' all prior knowledge. Heidegger proved that because the researcher's Dasein is inextricably embedded in the world, complete bracketing is ontologically impossible; instead, prior understandings (fore-structures: fore-having, fore-sight, fore-conception) must be acknowledged through transparent hermeneutic reflexivity.
2. The Hermeneutic Circle: Understanding unfolds through an ongoing iterative movement between the part and the whole: interpreting individual lived experiences within the broader cultural horizon of existence.
3. The Four Existentials (Lifeworld Guides - Van Manen):
   - Lived Space (Spatiality): How space is experienced subjectively (e.g., the suffocating feel of an ICU room).
   - Lived Body (Corporeality): How illness, aging, or performance is experienced bodily.
   - Lived Time (Temporality): Subjective time (e.g., the agonizing slow time of waiting for a biopsy result).
   - Lived Human Relation (Relationality): The interpersonal web of connection with others.
4. Everyday Coping (Ready-to-Hand vs. Present-at-Hand): Human beings engage with tools and environments seamlessly without conscious reflection (ready-to-hand); only when a breakdown occurs (present-at-hand) does explicit cognitive reflection emerge.
terms.benchmarks:
Phenomenological research standards (Heidegger, 1927; Van Manen, 2014; Smith et al., 2022):
- Epistemological Alignment: Hermeneutic phenomenological dissertations must declare Heideggerian or Gadamerian ontology, contrasting it with Husserlian transcendental phenomenology.
- Lifeworld Existential Framing: Qualitative findings are frequently organized and deepened using the four existential lifeworld guides (corporeality, spatiality, temporality, relationality).
- Pre-Reflective Data Capture: Interview prompts must focus on concrete lived memories and bodily sensations rather than intellectualized retrospective theories.
terms.pitfalls:
Common philosophical traps in phenomenological papers:
1. Husserl-Heidegger Confusion: Claiming to use Heidegger's Dasein while asserting that the researcher 'bracketed all biases to achieve pure objective description', which is an impossible philosophical contradiction.
2. Jargon Posturing Without Methodological Substance: Quoting Heidegger's esoteric terminology (Dasein, Throwness, Sorge) in Chapter 1 without linking it to the interview questions or thematic coding.
3. Over-Intellectualized Interviewing: Asking participants abstract 'why' questions, prompting them to provide philosophical essays rather than rich accounts of their concrete lived experiences.
terms.apa_reference: Van Manen, M. (2014). Phenomenology of practice: Meaning-giving methods in phenomenological research and writing. Left Coast Press.

terms.vietnamese: Tuyên bố tính sẵn có của dữ liệu (DAS)
vietnamese_variants: Tuyên bố khả dụng của dữ liệu
Cam kết chia sẻ dữ liệu nghiên cứu
terms.core_definition: A Data Availability Statement (DAS)—also termed a Data Access Statement—is a mandatory, standardized transparency disclosure required by international scholarly journals, publishers (Nature, Science, PLOS, Elsevier, Springer Nature), and research funders (Victoria Stodden et al., 2016). Positioned prominently within the published manuscript, the DAS explicitly informs readers, peer reviewers, and computational auditors whether, where, and under what conditions the underlying raw research data, analytical code, mathematical scripts, and supplementary materials supporting the published findings can be accessed, examined, and replicated.
terms.seminal_citation: Stodden, V., McNutt, M., Bailey, D. H., Deelman, E., Gil, Y., Hanson, B., Heroux, M. A., Ioannidis, J. P. A., & Taufer, M. (2016). Enhancing reproducibility for computational methods. Science, 354(6317), 1240-1241. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aah6168
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Data Availability Statement (DAS) according to Nature Portfolio (2016).
terms.operational_mechanism:
Standardized DAS classifications follow four primary tier models:
1. Open Repository Storage (Gold Standard): Data and analysis scripts are deposited in an open, trustworthy, DOI-assigning repository (e.g., OSF, Zenodo, Dryad, Figshare, Harvard Dataverse) with an explicit persistent identifier: 'The datasets generated and analyzed during the current study are available in the Zenodo repository, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.XXXXX'.
2. Embedded Supplementary Materials: Data and code are published directly as online supplementary files accompanying the article.
3. Restricted Access (Ethical, Legal, or Commercial Constraints): For sensitive medical, clinical, or proprietary corporate data where open sharing violates privacy or intellectual property: 'The data that support the findings of this study are available from [Third Party/Hospital], but restrictions apply to the availability of these data... available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request and with permission of [Ethics Committee]'.
4. Public Secondary Data Disclosures: For studies utilizing secondary datasets (e.g., Compustat, CRSP, World Bank, Kaggle): Explicitly citing the database name, provider, access date, and specific query parameters.
terms.benchmarks:
Open Science and publishing benchmarks (Stodden et al., 2016; Nature Portfolio / PLOS Guidelines):
- Universal Mandate: Top-tier journals enforce a strict DAS requirement; submissions lacking an explicit DAS are unsubmitted before peer review.
- Discredited Status of 'Upon Reasonable Request': Contemporary research shows that $> 80\%$ of authors who claim 'data available upon reasonable request' fail or refuse to provide data when requested; top journals actively discourage or ban this statement unless legally justified.
- FAIR Data Alignment: Repositories chosen must adhere to FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable).
terms.pitfalls:
Common compliance failures and ethical traps:
1. Phantom Repositories: Providing a repository link or private GitHub URL that becomes dead, password-locked, or deleted within 6 months of publication.
2. Violating Anonymization Commitments: Uploading raw interview transcripts or genomic data containing identifying demographic markers to open public repositories, violating participant confidentiality.
3. The False 'Proprietary' Excuse: Falsely claiming data cannot be shared due to 'corporate secrecy' when the company agreement explicitly permitted de-identified sharing.
terms.apa_reference: Nature Portfolio. (2021). Availability of data, materials, code and protocols: Policy guidelines. Springer Nature. https://www.nature.com/nature-portfolio/editorial-policies/reporting-standards

terms.term: Data Display in Qualitative Analysis (Miles, Huberman, & Saldaña)
terms.vietnamese: Trình bày dữ liệu trong phân tích định tính (Khung Miles, Huberman & Saldaña)
vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật trực quan hóa dữ liệu định tính
Ma trận và mạng lưới dữ liệu định tính
terms.core_definition: Data Display in Qualitative Analysis is the pivotal analytical stage in the classic qualitative data analysis framework formulated by Matthew B. Miles, A. Michael Huberman, and Johnny Saldaña (2014; Miles & Huberman, 1984, 1994). Rejecting the assumption that qualitative data must remain cumbersome, unwieldy walls of narrative text, Miles and Huberman established the foundational maxim: 'You know what you display.' A data display is an organized, compressed assembly of information—specifically structured as Matrices (rows and columns) or Networks (nodes and directional links)—that permits systematic cross-case comparison, pattern recognition, and robust conclusion drawing and verification.
terms.seminal_citation: Miles, M. B., & Huberman, A. M. (1984). Qualitative data analysis: A sourcebook of new methods. SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Data Display in Qualitative Analysis according to Miles & Huberman (1994).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The qualitative display architecture operates across two primary structural typologies:
1. Qualitative Matrices (Tabular Displays):
   - Role-Ordered Matrices: Sorting qualitative responses according to organizational roles or stakeholder hierarchies.
   - Time-Ordered / Chronological Matrices: Tracking events, strategic actions, and perceptual shifts over sequential chronological stages.
   - Concept-Ordered Matrices: Organizing data by theoretical categories, showing how specific themes manifest across diverse sites.
   - Effects Matrices: Systematically displaying ultimate outcomes and impacts following an intervention.
2. Qualitative Networks (Graphical Displays):
   - Causal Chains / Causal Networks: Directed graph diagrams where boxes represent variables/streams and arrows represent observed causal flows.
   - Cognitive Networks: Mapping managerial mental models and decision heuristics.
3. The Three Concurrent Analytical Streams: Data Condensation $\to$ Data Display $\to$ Conclusion Drawing & Verification. Data display is NOT a cosmetic post-hoc illustration; it is the core engine where analytical thinking occurs.
terms.benchmarks:
Analytical rigor benchmarks (Miles et al., 2014; Bazeley, 2018):
- Elimination of Text Clutter: Displays compress hundreds of transcript pages into a single visible 1-page matrix or network that can be viewed and audited at a single glance.
- Grounded Cell Entries: Matrix cells must contain concise thematic summaries, verbatim anchor quotes, or calibrated rating symbols, NOT empty platitudes.
- Iterative Refinement: Displays are constructed provisionally and redesigned iteratively as fieldwork and theoretical insights deepen.
terms.pitfalls:
Common qualitative reporting errors:
1. Purely Decorative Displays: Drawing an intricate network diagram for the published paper that was never used during actual data analysis to derive conclusions.
2. Information Overload: Constructing an unreadable matrix with 50 columns and 5-point microscopic font, destroying the visual comparative utility of the display.
3. Lack of Grounding in Matrices: Entering subjective researcher judgments into matrix cells without supporting verbatim participant quotes or field note citations.
terms.apa_reference: Miles, M. B., Huberman, A. M., & Saldaña, J. (2014). Qualitative data analysis: A methods sourcebook (3rd ed.). SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích bao màng dữ liệu
vietnamese_variants: Phân tích hiệu quả phi tham số DEA
Mô hình đường biên bao dữ liệu
terms.core_definition: Phân tích bao màng dữ liệu (Data Envelopment Analysis - DEA, được khởi xướng bởi Abraham Charnes, William W. Cooper và Edwardo Rhodes năm 1978 qua mô hình CCR kinh điển) là phương pháp tối ưu hóa toán học phi tham số (non-parametric linear programming) dùng để đánh giá hiệu quả hoạt động tương đối của tập hợp các đơn vị ra quyết định đồng nhất (Decision Making Units - DMUs, ví dụ: các chi nhánh ngân hàng, trường đại học, bệnh viện, phân xưởng sản xuất). Khác với các phương pháp tham số như Hồi quy OLS hay Phân tích biên ngẫu nhiên (SFA) vốn yêu cầu định trước dạng hàm sản xuất (Cobb-Douglas, Translog) và phân phối sai số, DEA không đòi hỏi bất kỳ giả định tiên nghiệm nào về hàm công nghệ. DEA xây dựng một đường biên sản xuất hiệu quả thực nghiệm (Empirical Production Frontier) bao bọc toàn bộ các điểm dữ liệu quan sát. Hiệu quả kỹ thuật của mỗi DMU được đo bằng khoảng cách tương đối từ vị trí của DMU đó đến đường biên hiệu quả.
terms.seminal_citation: Charnes, A., Cooper, W. W., & Rhodes, E. (1978). Measuring the efficiency of decision making units. European Journal of Operational Research, 2(6), 429-444.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) according to Charnes, Cooper & Rhodes (1978).
terms.short_definition: Kỹ thuật quy hoạch tuyến tính phi tham số đo lường hiệu quả kỹ thuật tương đối của các đơn vị ra quyết định đồng nhất có đa đầu vào và đa đầu ra.
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Xác định tập hợp DMUs và các biến số: Lựa chọn các đơn vị đồng nhất và xác định tập hợp đa đầu vào $X = (x_1, \dots, x_m)$ và đa đầu ra $Y = (y_1, \dots, y_s)$.
2. Lựa chọn định hướng mô hình:
   - Định hướng đầu vào (Input-oriented): Tối thiểu hóa lượng đầu vào sử dụng để đạt được mức đầu ra hiện tại cố định.
   - Định hướng đầu ra (Output-oriented): Tối đa hóa sản lượng đầu ra có thể tạo ra từ mức đầu vào sẵn có cố định.
3. Thiết lập bài toán quy hoạch tuyến tính (Mô hình CCR - Charnes et al., 1978):
   Đối với $DMU_0$, giải bài toán tối ưu hóa:
   $\max_{\mu, \nu} \theta = \sum_{r=1}^s \mu_r y_{r0}$ với ràng buộc $\sum_{i=1}^m \nu_i x_{i0} = 1$, $\sum_{r=1}^s \mu_r y_{rj} - \sum_{i=1}^m \nu_i x_{ij} \le 0, \forall j$, và $\mu_r, \nu_i \ge \epsilon > 0$.
4. Tính toán điểm số hiệu quả kỹ thuật (Technical Efficiency - TE):
   Điểm số $\theta$ luôn nằm trong khoảng $0 < \theta \le 1$. DMU đạt hiệu quả hoàn hảo nếu $\theta = 1$ và không có biến bù dư thừa (slacks = 0).
5. Xác định tập tham chiếu chuẩn (Peers / Benchmark set) và tính toán mục tiêu cải tiến (Targets): Đối với các DMU kém hiệu quả ($\theta < 1$), DEA cung cấp chính xác các đơn vị hình mẫu trên đường biên và lượng đầu vào cần cắt giảm hoặc đầu ra cần tăng thêm.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Điểm số hiệu quả kỹ thuật (TE Score): $\theta = 1.0$ (hay $100\%$) là đơn vị nằm trên đường biên hiệu quả; $\theta < 1.0$ là kém hiệu quả kỹ thuật.
2. Quy tắc kinh nghiệm về cỡ mẫu (Dyson et al., 2001; Cooper et al., 2007):
   - Số lượng DMUs $n$ tối thiểu phải thỏa mãn: $n \ge 3 \times (m + s)$, trong đó $m$ là số đầu vào, $s$ là số đầu ra.
   - Hoặc $n \ge \max\{m \times s, 3 \times (m + s)\}$. Nếu vi phạm, phần lớn các DMU sẽ bị đẩy lên điểm số 1.0 giả tạo do thiếu bậc tự do.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Nhạy cảm tuyệt đối với giá trị ngoại lai và sai số đo lường (Outlier Sensitivity): Do là phương pháp tất định phi tham số, DEA coi toàn bộ độ lệch khỏi đường biên đều là sự kém hiệu quả. Một điểm dị biệt do gõ nhầm dữ liệu có thể kéo đường biên lên cao bất thường và làm sai lệch điểm số của toàn bộ hệ thống.
2. Lạm dụng quá nhiều biến đầu vào/đầu ra trên cỡ mẫu nhỏ (Curse of Dimensionality): Càng đưa nhiều chỉ tiêu vào mô hình trong khi số lượng DMU ít, chiều không gian dữ liệu càng phình to, dẫn đến hiện tượng hầu hết các DMU đều trở thành 'độc nhất vô nhị' và đạt điểm hiệu quả 1.0 mà không phản ánh đúng năng lực thực tế.
3. Áp dụng hồi quy Tobit hai bước tùy tiện cho điểm số DEA: Điểm số DEA bị tương quan chuỗi phức tạp do cùng phụ thuộc vào đường biên chung. Simar & Wilson (2007) đã chứng minh hồi quy Tobit thông thường bị sai số trệch nghiêm trọng; bắt buộc phải sử dụng thuật toán hồi quy cắt cụt kèm Bootstrap lặp lại (Double Bootstrap Truncated Regression).
terms.apa_reference: Charnes, A., Cooper, W. W., & Rhodes, E. (1978). Measuring the efficiency of decision making units. European Journal of Operational Research, 2(6), 429-444. https://doi.org/10.1016/0377-2217(78)90138-8

terms.vietnamese: Kế hoạch quản lý dữ liệu (DMP)
vietnamese_variants: Kế hoạch quản trị dữ liệu khoa học
Data Management Plan in Grant Proposals
terms.core_definition: A Data Management Plan (DMP) is a formal, living document mandated by major national and international research funding agencies (such as the US National Science Foundation - NSF, National Institutes of Health - NIH, and European Commission Horizon Europe; William K.
